Ahoy there, me young mates! Gather round, gather round. Ye've come for a tale of high seas adventure, have ye? Well, ye're in luck. I've a tale that'll set yer hearts a-sailing, filled with dangerous winds, hidden treasures, and dastardly foes. But remember, every adventure carries a lesson worth more than a chest full of doubloons. So listen well.Years ago, when I was a swashbuckler myself, sailing under the Jolly Roger, our crew was on the hunt for the legendary treasure of Captain Redbeard. Stories whispered that he'd hidden a chest filled to the brim with gold and precious gems on a far-off island, protected by a beast of untold power.Our Captain, a fair but stern man by the name of Silvereye, was determined to find this treasure, not just for its worth, but to prove to himself and the world that he was a pirate worth his salt. And, so we set sail, using an old, tattered map Silvereye had won in a game of dice.Days turned into weeks, and weeks into months. We sailed through calm waters and raging storms, never losing sight of our goal. The crew's spirits were tested, but Silvereye's determination kept us going.Finally, we arrived at the island, a spit of land shrouded in mystery and fear. There was a mountain, a gaping maw of a cave at its base. Legend said the beast lived there. We drew lots to see who would face the beast, and as luck would have it, Silvereye drew the short straw.With a steely glint in his eye, he entered the cave, sword in hand. Hours passed, and we heard roars, clashing steel, and the echoes of a battle. Then, silence. We feared the worst. But just as dawn broke, Silvereye emerged, battered but victorious. In his hands, he held the glittering treasure chest.But here's the twist, young ones. We cheered, but Silvereye looked at us with weary eyes and said, "Aye, we've won the gold, but at what cost? Months at sea, battling the elements, risking our lives. And for what? A chest of gold? Is that the measure of a man? I've learned that it's not the treasure, but the journey that shapes us. The trials we face, the people we meet, the person we become...that's the real treasure."We were silent, the words sinking in. Silvereye, though a pirate, had imparted a wisdom greater than any we'd heard before.And that's the tale, me young shipmates. The lesson? Life's journey is full of treasures if we but look beyond the gold. Remember, it's not what you find at the end, but who you become along the way. Now, go on, explore these books, your own islands of adventure. And remember, every page turned is a step on your own journey. Make it count.

Hacker News is a social news website focusing on computer science and entrepreneurship. It was created by Paul Graham, a co-founder of Y Combinator, which is a prominent startup accelerator. The website's users can submit stories (or links to stories) and the community can upvote these submissions, similar to how Reddit operates. The highest-voted stories appear on the front page, ensuring that they get the most visibility.The site also supports comments on each story, where a lot of insightful discussion takes place. In terms of content, Hacker News tends to focus on technology, startups, programming languages, computer science breakthroughs, and broader societal implications of these areas.The community that frequents Hacker News is typically tech-savvy, with many of them working in the tech industry or related fields. The demographics often include software engineers, tech entrepreneurs, venture capitalists, digital nomads, data scientists, and more. A significant number of users are also interested in or associated with startups, given Y Combinator's pivotal role in the startup ecosystem.There is a strong culture of insightful commentary and discussion on the site. The users are generally very knowledgeable about the topics they discuss, and the level of discourse is usually quite high, albeit with the inevitable disagreements and debates that come with any online community.In terms of behavior and etiquette, Hacker News places a strong emphasis on respectful, thoughtful discussion. The site's guidelines ask users to refrain from name-calling and to respond to the strongest plausible interpretation of what someone says, rather than attacking weaker interpretations. This aim for constructive dialogue is part of what sets Hacker News apart from many other online communities.It's important to remember, however, that like any online community, Hacker News doesn't represent a single unified perspective. There's a wide range of viewpoints, experiences, and backgrounds represented in the community. So while you can expect a focus on technology and startups, you'll also see a diversity of perspectives on these topics.

这段代码创建了一个新的 String 类型的变量 name，并将其初始化为 "Alice"。让我们详细解释一下：let name: String：这部分代码声明了一个新的变量 name，并指定其类型为 String。String 是 Rust 中的一个类型，用于存储可变长度的 UTF-8 编码的字符串。String::from("Alice")：这部分代码调用了 String 类型的 from 函数，创建了一个新的 String 实例，其内容为 "Alice"。"Alice" 是一个字符串字面量，它的类型是 &str，这是 Rust 中的另一种字符串类型，通常用于存储固定长度的字符串。String::from 函数将这个 &str 类型的字符串字面量转换为 String 类型。所以，整个语句 let name: String = String::from("Alice"); 创建了一个新的 String 类型的变量 name，并将其初始化为 "Alice"。

是的，你的理解是正确的。当你创建一个 String 类型的变量时，Rust 会在堆内存中为字符串数据分配空间。这个 String 变量拥有这块内存，当 String 变量离开作用域时，Rust 会自动回收这块内存，这就是 Rust 的所有权（ownership）系统。例如，当你执行 let name: String = String::from("Alice"); 时，"Alice" 这个字符串会被存储在堆内存中，name 变量就拥有了这块内存。当 name 变量离开作用域时，Rust 会自动回收这块内存，以防止内存泄漏。另一方面，&str 类型的变量是对某个字符串数据的引用，它并不拥有这块内存。&str 类型的变量通常用于表示固定长度的字符串，例如字符串字面量。字符串字面量在编译时被存储在程序的二进制文件中，所以它们不需要动态分配内存。例如，当你执行 let name = "Alice"; 时，name 变量是一个对 "Alice" 这个字符串字面量的引用，它并不拥有这个字符串的内存。这个字符串在编译时就已经被存储在程序的二进制文件中了。总的来说，String 和 &str 都可以用来表示字符串，但它们在内存管理和功能上有一些重要的区别。你应该根据你的具体需求来选择使用哪种类型。

变量隐藏（Variable Shadowing）是 Rust 语言的一个特性，它在某些情况下可以使代码更简洁和易于理解。然而，过度或不当地使用变量隐藏可能会导致代码难以理解和维护，特别是在大型的工程项目中。以下是一些关于何时和何地使用变量隐藏的建议：类型转换：如果你需要将一个变量从一种类型转换为另一种类型，并且你不再需要原来的变量，那么使用变量隐藏可能是有意义的。例如，你可能需要将一个整数转换为字符串进行处理，然后你不再需要原来的整数。可变性转换：如果你需要将一个不可变的变量变为可变的，那么使用变量隐藏可能是有意义的。这可以避免你创建一个新的可变变量，并且需要为它找一个新的名字。避免不必要的新变量名：如果你需要对一个变量进行一系列的操作，并且每次操作都会产生一个新的值，那么使用变量隐藏可以避免你为每个中间值创建一个新的变量名。然而，在大型的工程项目中，过度或不当地使用变量隐藏可能会导致代码难以理解和维护。如果一个变量在代码的不同部分有不同的类型或值，那么阅读和理解代码可能会变得困难。在这种情况下，使用不同的变量名可能会更清晰，更易于理解。总的来说，变量隐藏是一个强大的工具，但应谨慎使用，以避免混淆和错误。你应该根据你的具体需求和情况来决定是否使用变量隐藏。

Rust 的命名约定推荐使用下划线（snake case）来命名函数、变量和模块。这是由 Rust 的官方样式指南推荐的，主要有以下几个原因：一致性：在 Rust 社区中，大家都遵循这个命名约定，这样可以使代码更易于阅读和理解。当你阅读其他人的 Rust 代码，或者其他人阅读你的 Rust 代码时，你们都可以期望看到相同的命名样式。可读性：下划线可以清楚地分隔单词，使得长名称更易于阅读。例如，my_long_variable 比 myLongVariable 或 mylongvariable 更易于阅读。与 Rust 的其他部分保持一致：Rust 的一些关键字，如 self 和 super，以及一些预定义类型，如 i32 和 str，都是小写的。使用下划线连接的命名可以与这些关键字和类型保持一致。请注意，这只是一个约定，而不是一个强制的规则。你可以选择使用其他的命名样式，但遵循这个约定可以使你的代码更符合 Rust 社区的期望，更易于与其他 Rust 程序员合作。

Based on the information provided, "Vectoring in Research," as presented in Stanford's CS 197 & 197C course by Sean Liu & Lauren Gillespie, refers to an approach or methodology for tackling complex research projects. Here's a summarized interpretation of the concept:Vectoring is an iterative process used in research to identify and focus on the most critical aspect, or "dimension of risk," in a project at a given time. This critical aspect is called a "vector."The process is not linear, where you start with an idea and then simply work towards a final result. Instead, research is an exploration where vectoring helps guide the path and prioritize tasks.The goal of vectoring is to manage and reduce risk and uncertainty. Instead of trying to solve all aspects of a problem simultaneously, researchers pick one vector (dimension of uncertainty) and focus on reducing its risk and uncertainty within a short time frame, typically 1-2 weeks.The concept advocates an iterative approach, where after one vector's risk is mitigated, new vectors (risks or uncertainties) might emerge. Then, the process of vectoring is repeated for the new vector. This continuous re-vectoring allows researchers to keep honing the core insights of the research project.Different vectors might imply building different parts of your system or project, but instead of building all at once, you reduce uncertainty in the most important dimension first and then build out from there.The vectoring process involves generating and ranking questions based on their criticality, then rapidly answering the most critical question. This approach is often supplemented by assumption mapping, which is a strategy for articulating and ranking questions based on their importance and the level of known information.Successful vectoring enables rapid iteration cycles and a focused approach, which allows researchers to efficiently work through complex problems and avoid getting overwhelmed by trying to solve everything at once.In summary, Vectoring in Research is a method to manage complexity and risk in research projects by focusing on the most significant risks or uncertainties, reducing them, and then moving on to the next most important risk or uncertainty, in a continuous iterative process.

"Known unknowns" and "unknown unknowns" are terms used in risk management and project planning. They refer to different types of uncertainties that one might encounter in a project or task. Understanding these concepts can help in identifying, managing, and mitigating risks effectively.Known Unknowns: These are uncertainties or risks that we are aware of but do not know the outcome. For example, we might know that a particular phase of a project will have challenges because we are using a new technology or method, but we don't know what specific issues might arise or how severe they will be. This uncertainty is 'known' because we're aware of its existence, even though we don't know the details or implications. In project management, these risks are often identified during the planning phase and are accounted for by building in contingencies, such as additional time or resources, to manage them.Unknown Unknowns: These are risks or uncertainties that we're not even aware exist, so we cannot plan for them. For instance, during a construction project, an unknown unknown might be an archaeological discovery on the construction site that halts work. These are unpredictable risks that were not foreseen and could not have been reasonably predicted. Since we can't identify these risks in advance, we can't plan for them directly. Instead, we manage these risks indirectly by ensuring that our project plans are flexible and adaptable, and that we have the capacity to respond effectively to unexpected events when they occur.Understanding these concepts allows project managers and team members to better prepare for the unexpected. It encourages teams to build in buffers for known unknowns and to remain adaptable and responsive to handle unknown unknowns. It also underscores the fact that no matter how thoroughly a project is planned, there will always be an element of uncertainty. This understanding can help foster a more realistic and resilient approach to project management.

In the context of freight and shipping, a consignee refers to the person, company, or entity that is designated to receive a shipment or cargo. The consignee is typically specified by the shipper or the sender of the goods at the time of arranging transportation. The consignee can be an individual, a business, a warehouse, a distribution center, or any other location where the shipment is intended to be delivered.The consignee's role is to take possession of the goods upon arrival, verify the contents of the shipment, and handle any necessary documentation or customs procedures for clearance. They are responsible for inspecting the goods for damage or discrepancies and reporting any issues to the carrier or the shipper. The consignee may also be responsible for paying any applicable duties, taxes, or fees associated with the importation of the goods.It's worth noting that the terms and responsibilities related to consignees can vary depending on the specific shipping terms agreed upon between the shipper and the consignee. These terms are typically outlined in the shipping contract or the bill of lading, which govern the rights and obligations of both parties involved in the transportation of the goods.

"Load on, load off" freight refers to a specific type of cargo handling method commonly used in maritime shipping. It is also known as "lo-lo" or "lift-on/lift-off" freight.In this method, cargo is loaded and unloaded from a ship using specialized equipment such as cranes or gantry systems. The cargo is lifted off the ship's deck or from a dock and placed onto the port or terminal. Similarly, when loading, the cargo is lifted from the port or terminal and placed onto the ship.Load on, load off (LOLO) freight is commonly used for shipping containers, heavy machinery, oversized cargo, or any other items that cannot be easily rolled on or off the vessel. It allows for efficient loading and unloading of goods, making it a preferred method for many types of cargo that require special handling.This method contrasts with "roll-on/roll-off" (Ro-Ro) freight, where cargo can be driven or towed directly onto and off the ship using ramps or specialized vehicles. Ro-Ro is typically used for vehicles, such as cars, trucks, and trailers.Both load on, load off and roll-on/roll-off methods offer advantages depending on the type of cargo being transported and the specific requirements of the shipping process.

In the context of freight, an insurance provider refers to a company or entity that offers insurance coverage specifically for freight or cargo shipments. Freight insurance is designed to protect the value of goods being transported against various risks and perils that can occur during transit, such as theft, damage, loss, or other unforeseen circumstances.Insurance providers specializing in freight or cargo insurance work with businesses, freight forwarders, logistics companies, and individuals involved in the transportation of goods. They offer different types of insurance policies tailored to meet the specific needs of their clients. These policies may cover a wide range of transportation modes, including shipping by sea, air, rail, or truck.Insurance providers for freight typically offer two primary types of coverage:All-Risk Coverage: This type of insurance provides comprehensive protection for goods during transit, covering a broad range of risks and perils. All-risk coverage generally offers more extensive protection but may have certain exclusions or limitations specified in the policy.Named Perils Coverage: With this type of coverage, specific risks or perils are listed in the policy, and the insurance will only cover losses caused by those named perils. Common named perils may include fire, theft, collision, overturning of the vehicle, natural disasters, and others.Freight insurance providers assess the value of the cargo, the shipping route, the mode of transportation, and various other factors to determine the cost of the insurance coverage. They also establish terms and conditions, including deductibles, coverage limits, and specific exclusions.It's important for businesses and individuals involved in freight transportation to work with reputable and experienced insurance providers to ensure adequate coverage and protection for their cargo throughout the transportation process.

An air shipment, also known as air freight or air cargo, has several attributes that are essential for its successful transportation. Here are some key attributes typically associated with air shipments:Weight and Size: Air shipments must comply with weight and size restrictions imposed by airlines. Different airlines may have varying limitations, and exceeding them can result in additional fees or even rejection of the shipment. It's important to adhere to the guidelines provided by the airline or freight forwarder.Packaging: Proper packaging is crucial to ensure the safety and integrity of the goods during air transportation. The packaging should protect the contents from damage, shifting, or any external elements that could impact the shipment. It should also meet the specific requirements of the airline and any regulatory bodies involved.Documentation: Air shipments require various documents to facilitate customs clearance and compliance with international trade regulations. These documents may include airway bills, commercial invoices, packing lists, export licenses, certificates of origin, and any other relevant paperwork based on the nature of the goods and destination country requirements.Security: Due to the stringent security measures associated with air transportation, it is important to ensure the security of air shipments. Compliance with regulations such as the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) security standards is necessary. This may involve using tamper-evident packaging, providing accurate cargo descriptions, and adhering to any additional security screening procedures.Transit Time: One of the advantages of air shipments is their relatively faster transit time compared to other modes of transport. Air freight is ideal for time-sensitive or perishable goods. However, it is crucial to consider the transit time when planning the shipment and aligning it with the expected delivery requirements.Insurance: It is advisable to have appropriate insurance coverage for air shipments to protect against potential loss, damage, or theft during transit. While airlines may have liability limits for cargo, acquiring additional insurance coverage can provide extra peace of mind.Special Handling Requirements: Some goods may have specific handling requirements due to their nature, such as hazardous materials, perishable items, or fragile goods. Compliance with relevant regulations, proper labeling, and adherence to any temperature control or handling instructions are essential to ensure the safe transport of such goods.Customs and Regulatory Compliance: Air shipments must comply with customs regulations and trade laws of the origin and destination countries. It is crucial to provide accurate and complete customs documentation, pay any applicable duties or taxes, and comply with any import or export restrictions or licensing requirements.It's important to note that specific requirements and regulations may vary depending on the country, airline, and type of goods being shipped. Working with an experienced freight forwarder or logistics provider can help ensure that all necessary attributes and considerations are addressed for a successful air shipment.

An ocean shipment typically requires several attributes to facilitate the transportation of goods by sea. Here are some essential attributes associated with an ocean shipment:Shipping Container: Goods transported by ocean usually need to be properly packed and secured in standardized shipping containers. These containers come in various sizes and types, such as 20-foot or 40-foot containers, depending on the volume and nature of the cargo.Shipping Documentation: Various documents are necessary for an ocean shipment, including a bill of lading, commercial invoice, packing list, and any required permits or certificates. These documents provide information about the goods being shipped, their origin, destination, and other relevant details.Freight Forwarder/Shipping Agent: A freight forwarder or shipping agent plays a crucial role in organizing and coordinating the ocean shipment. They handle the logistics, documentation, customs requirements, and other aspects of the transportation process on behalf of the shipper.Carrier and Vessel: An ocean shipment requires a shipping carrier, which is typically a shipping line or a container vessel operator. The carrier operates the vessels that transport the cargo across the ocean. The shipper or freight forwarder arranges the booking with the carrier to secure space on the vessel.Port of Loading and Port of Discharge: The ocean shipment involves identifying the specific ports of loading and discharge. The port of loading is where the cargo is loaded onto the vessel, while the port of discharge is the destination port where the cargo will be unloaded.Customs Clearance: Customs procedures and clearance are an integral part of an ocean shipment. The shipper or the appointed customs broker must comply with customs regulations of both the origin and destination countries to facilitate the smooth movement of the cargo.Insurance: Shippers often opt for marine cargo insurance to protect their goods against potential loss or damage during transit. Insurance coverage can be arranged through insurance brokers or freight forwarders.Freight Rates and Charges: The cost of an ocean shipment includes freight rates and various charges, such as port handling charges, documentation fees, customs duties, and any additional services required, such as warehousing or inland transportation.Transit Time and Schedule: The transit time, or the duration it takes for the cargo to reach the destination, is an important attribute of an ocean shipment. Shippers need to consider the schedule and estimated arrival time to plan their logistics and meet customer demands.Tracking and Tracing: Many shipping lines and freight forwarders provide online tracking and tracing systems, allowing shippers to monitor the progress of their ocean shipments. This provides visibility and helps in managing supply chain operations effectively.It's important to note that specific requirements and attributes of an ocean shipment may vary depending on the nature of the goods, the trade route, the countries involved, and any applicable regulations or agreements.

Specialty shipping methods for freight refer to specialized transportation options designed to handle specific types of cargo or address unique shipping requirements. Here are some common specialty shipping methods for freight:Refrigerated Shipping: Also known as "reefer shipping," this method involves transporting perishable goods, such as food products, pharmaceuticals, or chemicals, in temperature-controlled containers or trailers to maintain a specific temperature range throughout transit.Oversized or Heavy Haul Shipping: This method is utilized for transporting large, heavy, or oversized cargo that exceeds the standard size and weight limits. It typically requires specialized equipment, permits, and sometimes escort vehicles to ensure safety and compliance with regulations.Hazardous Materials Shipping: Hazardous materials, such as flammable substances, toxic chemicals, or radioactive materials, require strict compliance with safety regulations. Specialized carriers are equipped and certified to handle the transportation of hazardous goods safely.Project Cargo Shipping: Project cargo refers to large-scale, complex shipments that require customized transportation solutions. It includes heavy machinery, construction equipment, oversized structures, or other specialized goods. These shipments often involve intricate planning, specialized equipment, and coordination with various stakeholders.Flatbed Shipping: Flatbed trucks are used to transport cargo that cannot be accommodated in standard enclosed trailers. This method is suitable for transporting oversized items, machinery, vehicles, construction materials, or other goods that require open-air transportation.Intermodal Shipping: Intermodal shipping involves using multiple modes of transportation, such as rail, truck, and sea, to transport freight. This method offers flexibility, cost-effectiveness, and reduced handling of cargo by utilizing standardized shipping containers that can seamlessly transition between different modes of transport.LTL (Less Than Truckload) Shipping: LTL shipping is utilized when the shipment's size does not require a full truckload. It involves combining multiple smaller shipments from different shippers into a single truckload to optimize efficiency and cost-effectiveness.Air Freight: Air freight is a fast and efficient shipping method for time-sensitive or high-value cargo. It is commonly used for perishable goods, pharmaceuticals, electronics, or urgent shipments that require swift transportation across long distances.Rail Freight: Rail transportation is suitable for shipping bulk commodities, such as coal, grains, or minerals, over long distances. It offers cost advantages, high capacity, and lower carbon emissions compared to other modes of transportation.These are just a few examples of specialty shipping methods for freight. The choice of shipping method depends on the nature of the cargo, transportation requirements, budget, and time constraints. Freight forwarders and logistics providers can assist in determining the most appropriate shipping method for specific needs.

A Transportation Management System (TMS) is a software application or platform that helps businesses efficiently manage and optimize their transportation and logistics operations. It is commonly used by companies involved in shipping, supply chain management, and distribution to streamline the process of planning, executing, and tracking the movement of goods.A TMS typically provides a wide range of features and functionalities to assist with transportation management, including:Shipment Planning: It helps in creating optimized plans for shipments, considering factors such as delivery deadlines, carrier availability, mode of transportation, and cost considerations.Carrier Selection and Freight Rate Management: TMS allows businesses to compare and select the most suitable carriers based on various criteria such as service level, cost, reliability, and transit times. It also facilitates managing freight rates and contracts with different carriers.Route Optimization: TMS software optimizes the routing of shipments to minimize transportation costs and improve efficiency. It considers variables like distance, traffic conditions, delivery time windows, and vehicle capacity to suggest the most efficient routes.Load Optimization: TMS assists in optimizing the utilization of transportation resources by consolidating shipments, maximizing vehicle capacity, and reducing empty miles. This helps reduce costs and environmental impact.Execution and Tracking: It enables the execution and tracking of transportation operations in real-time. TMS provides visibility into shipments, allowing businesses to monitor their movement, receive status updates, and proactively manage any exceptions or delays.Documentation and Compliance: TMS software helps automate the generation of shipping documents such as bills of lading, customs forms, and delivery receipts. It also ensures compliance with regulatory requirements and industry standards.Analytics and Reporting: TMS generates comprehensive reports and analytics on transportation performance, costs, carrier performance, delivery times, and other key metrics. This data helps businesses identify areas for improvement and make informed decisions.By leveraging a TMS, businesses can enhance their transportation efficiency, reduce costs, improve customer service, and gain better control over their supply chain operations. It enables centralized management of transportation processes, enhances visibility, and automates manual tasks, resulting in increased productivity and operational effectiveness.

In the context of freight and logistics, EDI stands for Electronic Data Interchange. It refers to the electronic exchange of business documents and information between different parties involved in the freight industry, such as shippers, carriers, freight forwarders, and customs agencies.EDI enables the transfer of structured data electronically in a standardized format, allowing for efficient and automated communication between trading partners. It eliminates the need for manual data entry, paper-based documentation, and traditional communication methods like fax or email. EDI helps streamline various freight-related processes, including order placement, shipment tracking, customs documentation, invoicing, and payment reconciliation.By using EDI, freight companies can achieve greater accuracy, speed, and visibility in their operations. It promotes seamless information flow, reduces errors and delays, and enhances overall supply chain efficiency. EDI standards, such as ANSI X12 and UN/EDIFACT, define the specific formats and protocols for data exchange, ensuring compatibility and interoperability between different systems and organizations.Overall, EDI plays a crucial role in modern freight management, facilitating the exchange of data and streamlining processes to support timely and reliable delivery of goods.

Título do artigo: "Narrativas Digitais: Como Sistemas Conectados Estão Mudando Nosso Senso de Tempo e Espaço"Na era pré-digital, a vida era mais simples, mais tangível. Imagem uma fazenda isolada, onde o acordar não é ditado por um alarme em um dispositivo eletrônico, mas pelo cantar do galo e o nascer do sol. Nessa fazenda, o café é feito no fogão a lenha, e a conexão mais importante do dia é com a natureza. Cada evento que acontece é palpável, local, ligado a um ciclo natural e rítmico. Pode ser um bezerro nascendo, uma maçã caindo da árvore. Não existe uma expectativa de sequência, apenas a aceitação do fluxo da vida.Contraste essa vida com a que vivemos hoje, onde os eventos e as informações são amplificados e acelerados pelo mundo digital. Estamos sempre conectados, sempre atentos. O "cantar do galo" vem de um telefone celular ou de um relógio, repetindo várias vezes ao dia de acordo com várias agendas simultâneas. Nós não apenas consumimos informações de uma maneira quase incessante, como também temos a capacidade de agir, tanto localmente quanto em escala global.Nesse contexto, o conceito de narrativas digitais surge com grande relevância. As plataformas digitais, como Facebook, TikTok e tantas outras, não apenas fornecem informações, mas também criam narrativas que tentam capturar e manter nossa atenção. Essas plataformas desenvolveram algoritmos sofisticados que aprendem com nossos comportamentos e preferências para gerar narrativas que acreditam ser do nosso interesse.Um exemplo disso pode ser observado em eventos como feiras e conferências. Quando um vendedor passa um leitor de código de barras no seu crachá e pergunta "posso te tagear?", ele está abrindo um novo capítulo na narrativa digital que envolve você e a empresa dele. A partir daí, você começa a receber mensagens que tentam criar uma conexão, construir um relacionamento, através de uma sequência de "episódios". Essa sequência não é aleatória, mas é projetada para levar a um desfecho desejado - talvez uma compra ou uma nova parceria.Essas narrativas digitais são projetadas para serem viciantes. Empregam técnicas de gamificação, liberando doses de dopamina quando alcançamos certos "marcos" ou "recompensas". Isso cria um ciclo de feedback positivo, incentivando-nos a continuar interagindo com a plataforma ou com a narrativa.No entanto, essas narrativas não são necessariamente relevantes para nosso trabalho ou nossa vida pessoal. Apesar disso, nos envolvem, nos enchem, até sentirmos que estamos "sem tempo", mesmo que não estejamos necessariamente "usando muito tempo". O custo é uma sensação de esgotamento, de falta de energia para fazer algo que pode ser verdadeiramente importante para nós.A questão-chave é entender como podemos usar o poder das narrativas digitais a nosso favor, ao invés de sermos guiados por elas. E, talvez mais importante, como podemos recuperar o nosso tempo e a nossa atenção, restabelecendo uma conexão mais saudável com o mundo digital e com nós mesmos.

A cada dia, o canto do galo é substituído por um alarme no celular ou no relógio, ecoando em ritmo com uma ou mais agendas simultâneas. Nossas vidas, antes delimitadas pelo ambiente local, expandiram-se para o cenário global graças à era digital.Ao retornar a uma fazenda isolada do ritmo moderno, poderíamos observar um dia moldado por eventos locais e tangíveis. A era digital, no entanto, expandiu radicalmente nossas entradas e saídas de informações. As notificações que recebemos trazem consigo narrativas que, embora possam ser irrelevantes para o nosso trabalho, nos sobrecarregam e nos fazem sentir sem tempo.Se você é um empreendedor - seja um iniciante com uma startup, um veterano administrando uma corporação ou alguém empreendendo na própria vida - provavelmente se encontra no olho deste turbilhão. Por isso, convido-o a refletir sobre a urgência desenfreada em que vivemos e a considerar uma abordagem mais saudável para alcançar seus objetivos. Não devemos correr contra o tempo, mas sim aprender a interpretar e responder aos eventos ao nosso redor de uma maneira mais ponderada.Para entender melhor o início de nossa aceleração, peço que nos transportemos para 10 de Novembro de 1876. Nessa data, o imperador do Brasil, Dom Pedro II, ativou o gigantesco motor Corliss durante a inauguração da exposição do centenário da independência dos Estados Unidos, na Pensilvânia, Filadélfia. Esse marco simboliza o início da era em que vivemos agora, uma era em que as coisas se aceleraram.Este livro é uma jornada para desacelerar, entender a inundação de narrativas digitais que nos confrontam diariamente e encontrar um equilíbrio nessa tempestade de informações."Desta forma, seu prefácio mantém a mensagem central, mas se torna mais enxuto e focado no conceito de desacelerar. Também incluí uma transição suave para o capítulo que descreve o início da aceleração com o evento histórico do motor Corliss. As discussões mais detalhadas sobre narrativas digitais e o impacto dos sistemas conectados de terceiros podem ser exploradas em maior profundidade nos capítulos seguintes ou no artigo que estamos elaborando.

The use of await import(...) and import ... in JavaScript serve different purposes and have different implications. Here are a few points to consider:Loading type: Regular import ... statements are static imports. They load modules at startup, before the module's code is evaluated. This means that all the dependencies are loaded upfront, which can increase the initial loading time if you have many dependencies or large ones.On the other hand, await import(...) is a dynamic import. It loads modules on demand, during the runtime of the module's code. This means you can conditionally load modules, or delay their loading until they're actually needed. This can decrease the initial loading time and memory consumption, at the expense of possibly introducing loading delays later on.Top-level await: As of my knowledge cutoff in September 2021, await can only be used within an async function in JavaScript. This restriction has been relaxed in some environments, allowing top-level await, but it is not universally supported. So if you're working in an environment that doesn't support top-level await, you cannot use await import(...) outside of an async function. For maximum compatibility, you might need to use a static import instead.Error handling: If a static import fails to load a module (for example, if the module file is not found), the whole module fails to load, and any code that imports it will not run. In contrast, if a dynamic import fails, it returns a rejected Promise. This means that you can catch and handle the error using .catch() or a try/catch block. Depending on your needs, one or the other might be more suitable.Refactoring tools: Some code editors and refactoring tools have better support for static imports than dynamic imports. For example, they might be able to analyze static imports to determine which modules are no longer used, or to automatically update import paths when a module is moved. Dynamic imports are harder to analyze in this way.Overall, whether you should use await import(...) or import ... depends on the specifics of your project and its requirements.

ワードの検出時に投稿表示を強制的に終了する方法は、実装するシステムやプログラムによって異なります。以下にいくつかの一般的な手法を示しますが、具体的な要件に応じてカスタマイズする必要があります。フロントエンド側での検出と処理: ユーザーの入力をリアルタイムで監視し、禁止ワードが含まれている場合に投稿表示を終了させることができます。JavaScriptやフレームワークによっては、入力欄の変更イベントや送信ボタンのクリックイベントなどをフックして検出処理を行い、必要なアクションを実行することができます。バックエンドでの検出とフィルタリング: サーバーサイドで投稿を受け取った後に禁止ワードを検出し、必要なら投稿を終了させることができます。プログラミング言語やフレームワークに応じて、文字列のマッチングや正規表現などを使用して禁止ワードを検出し、処理を行います。検出された場合にはエラーメッセージを返すか、投稿を単に無視するかなど、目的に応じたアクションを選択します。データベースレベルでの制御: 禁止ワードのリストをデータベースに保持し、データベースレベルでフィルタリングを行うことも可能です。投稿がデータベースに格納される前に、禁止ワードが含まれているかどうかをチェックし、必要ならば処理を行います。これらの手法は、単体で使用するか、組み合わせて利用することができます。また、ワードの検出や処理の詳細は、使用している技術スタックや要件によって異なるため、具体的な実装方法については詳細な情報が必要です。

掲示板アプリで禁止ワードが出た場合、以下の手順を参考にして投稿表示を強制終了させる方法を実装することができます。フロントエンドでの検出と処理:ユーザーの入力を監視し、禁止ワードが含まれているかどうかを検出します。入力フィールドの変更イベントや送信ボタンのクリックイベントなどをフックして、検出処理を実行します。禁止ワードが検出された場合、投稿の送信を中止し、エラーメッセージを表示します。バックエンドでの検出とフィルタリング:サーバーサイドで投稿を受け取った後、禁止ワードを検出します。文字列のマッチングや正規表現を使用して、禁止ワードを検出します。禁止ワードが検出された場合、投稿を無視し、エラーメッセージを返します。データベースレベルでの制御:データベースに禁止ワードのリストを保持します。投稿がデータベースに格納される前に、禁止ワードが含まれているかどうかをチェックします。禁止ワードが検出された場合、投稿を無視し、エラーメッセージを返します。具体的な実装方法は、使用している技術スタックやフレームワークに依存しますが、上記の手順は一般的なアプローチです。フロントエンドとバックエンドの両方で検出処理を行うことで、ユーザーエクスペリエンスを向上させることができます。また、検出された禁止ワードに関する詳細な情報をログに記録することもおすすめです。

What you're describing is known as neuroevolution, a form of machine learning that uses evolutionary algorithms to train artificial neural networks. More specifically, it seems like you're interested in a particular type of neuroevolution called Genetic Algorithms.Here's a more technical description of your proposed approach:You aim to develop a neuroevolutionary approach to training a neural network to play Flappy Bird. This would begin with an initial population of neural networks, each with randomly initialized weights and biases.During each generation, these neural networks would play the game, and their performance would be evaluated, typically based on their score or longevity in the game.Next, a selection process would be conducted, which is inspired by natural selection. The best-performing neural networks—those with the highest fitness scores—are selected as parents for the next generation. This process is known as "selection."These selected networks would then be subject to genetic operations, such as crossover (also known as reproduction) and mutation. In the crossover stage, "offspring" neural networks are produced by combining the weights and biases of the parent networks. During mutation, some of these weights and biases are randomly altered to introduce variability and prevent premature convergence on suboptimal solutions.This new generation of networks, which comprises both the offspring and mutated versions of the highest-performing networks from the previous generation, would then be used in the next iteration of the process.The process repeats over many generations, progressively evolving the population toward better and better solutions, until a satisfactory solution (in this case, a neural network that can play Flappy Bird effectively) is found or a set number of generations is reached.The goal of this process is to leverage the power of natural evolution, effectively conducting a search through the space of possible solutions (i.e., the set of possible weights and biases for the network) to find a solution that maximizes the performance of the neural network on the task at hand.

Yes, you are correct that weights in a neural network are used to give each input feature a certain importance and that biases are used to offset the final activation value of the neuron.In a neural network, the bias is essentially a constant that is added to the product of the inputs and their corresponding weights before the activation function is applied. It allows for a shift in the activation function, enabling the neuron to fit the data better.In terms of necessity, while it is theoretically possible to train a neural network without biases, it's not commonly done because biases provide flexibility and help the network fit the data more accurately.Without the bias, each neuron's output would be a function strictly of the inputs. This means the decision boundary would always go through the origin (in a binary classification case, for example), which can severely limit the ability of the network to learn complex patterns.With a bias term, the network can adjust the outputs independently of the inputs, providing a much richer and more flexible function approximation capability. It effectively allows the activation function to be shifted left or right, which can be critical for successful learning. Thus, it is generally beneficial to include biases in your neural network models.

In many general explanations or introductory resources, the bias term may not be mentioned because it simplifies the understanding of the basic concepts of a neural network. It's often easier to understand the fundamental mechanism of a neural network — input features being multiplied by weights and passed through an activation function — without also introducing the concept of a bias.However, in practice, most neural networks do use biases. The bias is an important component of the neural network that helps to increase the flexibility of the model to fit the data. Without the bias term, the neuron is restricted in its ability to represent and solve problems.To be specific, even though weights handle the influence of input data, biases allow you to shift the activation function to the left or right, which can be critical because it helps the network represent patterns that are not centered around zero.It's worth noting that in the field of machine learning, you'll often see a trend of starting with simpler models or explanations, and then progressively adding complexity as understanding improves. So, it's not uncommon to initially discuss neural networks in terms of weights alone, and then later introduce the concept of biases.

Designing the architecture of a neural network is often more of an art than a science, and it depends heavily on the specific problem at hand. However, for a simple problem like the one you've described, you could start with a small and simple network and then iteratively refine it based on its performance.Given that you have two inputs (X and Y distance from the obstacle) and one binary output (flap or not), you could start with a single hidden layer. This is often a good starting point for simple problems, and it can be surprising how powerful even a single layer can be.As for the number of neurons in the hidden layer, a common heuristic is to choose a number between the size of the input layer (2 in your case) and the size of the output layer (1 in your case). So, you might start with a hidden layer of size 2 (the same size as the input layer).Therefore, a minimal starting point for your network could look like this:Input layer: 2 neurons (corresponding to the X and Y distances)Hidden layer: 2 neuronsOutput layer: 1 neuron (representing the decision to flap or not)After implementing this basic version, you can start to experiment. You might try adding more neurons to the hidden layer, adding additional hidden layers, or tweaking other hyperparameters of the model. Remember, each problem is unique, and the optimal network architecture will depend on the specifics of the problem. In this case, you'd be looking for an architecture that can learn to effectively play Flappy Bird.Finally, remember to carefully monitor the performance of your model both during and after training to avoid overfitting. This is when the model learns the training data too well and performs poorly on unseen data. In the context of a game, overfitting could mean the model plays one level extremely well but fails on others because it has essentially memorized the first level rather than learning the general mechanics of the game.

The specific weights and biases that would create this behavior can be difficult to specify exactly without actually running a training process, as the optimal weights and biases will depend on many factors, including the specifics of how the input data is normalized, the precise behavior of the game, and so on.However, I can try to give a simplified example that might give you some intuition. For simplicity, let's assume that both inputs (the X and Y distances) are normalized to be between -1 and 1.Let's say we have two neurons in the hidden layer. The first neuron could be responsible for detecting whether the bird is below the desired height. If Y is negative (meaning the bird is below the sweet spot), this neuron would fire, suggesting that the bird should flap. The second neuron could be responsible for detecting whether the bird is close enough to the obstacle (X is small).So the weights and biases for the hidden layer might look something like this:Neuron 1: weight for Y = -1 (negative because we want the neuron to fire when Y is negative), weight for X = 0 (we don't care about X for this neuron), bias = 0.5 (to adjust the firing threshold)Neuron 2: weight for Y = 0 (we don't care about Y for this neuron), weight for X = -1 (we want the neuron to fire when X is small, which means close to -1 in our normalized scale), bias = 0.5 (to adjust the firing threshold)Then, in the output layer, we could simply add up the outputs of these two neurons. If either of them fires, the bird should flap. This could be achieved with weights of 1 and a bias of -0.5 in the output layer (so the output is positive if either neuron fires).This is a very simplified example, and the actual weights and biases that would work best in practice would probably be different and would ideally be learned through the training process. Additionally, it's worth noting that in practice, you would typically use some kind of non-linear activation function in your neurons, which I haven't included in this simplified example.

with open('posts.json', 'a') as file: は、ファイルの読み書きに関するPythonの構文です。この構文を使用することで、ファイルを開いて操作を行い、処理が終了したら自動的にファイルを閉じることができます。具体的には、open() 関数を使用してファイルを開き、as キーワードを使ってファイルオブジェクトを変数 file に割り当てています。ここで、'posts.json' は開きたいファイルのパスを指定します。'a'は、ファイルを追記モード（append mode）で開くことを意味します。ファイルを追記モードで開くと、既存のファイルの内容を保持しつつ、新しいデータをファイルに追加できます。ファイルが存在しない場合は新しく作成されます。with 文のブロック内でファイルに対する操作を行います。例えば、file.write('data') のようにファイルにデータを書き込むことができます。ファイルへの書き込みや読み込みの操作を行った後、with ブロックを抜けると、ファイルは自動的に閉じられます。これにより、ファイルを明示的に閉じるための file.close() の呼び出しを省略することができます。with open('posts.json', 'a') as file: の構文を使用することで、ファイルの操作が終了した後でも正しくファイルを閉じることができるため、エラーのリスクを低減することができます。

ファイルを操作する際に使用できるいくつかの一般的なファイルモードがあります。以下にいくつかのモードを示します：読み込みモード（'r'）:open() 関数のデフォルトのモードです。ファイルを読み取るために使用されます。ファイルが存在しない場合はエラーが発生します。書き込みモード（'w'）:ファイルに書き込むために使用されます。ファイルが存在しない場合は新しいファイルが作成されます。ファイルが既に存在する場合は、既存の内容が上書きされます。追記モード（'a'）:ファイルの末尾に追記するために使用されます。ファイルが存在しない場合は新しいファイルが作成されます。ファイルが既に存在する場合は、既存の内容が保持されたまま新しいデータが追加されます。読み書きモード（'r+'）:ファイルを読み書きするために使用されます。ファイルが存在しない場合はエラーが発生します。ファイルが既に存在する場合は、読み取りと書き込みの両方が可能です。これらは一般的なモードの一部ですが、他にもいくつかのモードがあります。モードを指定することで、ファイルを開く際の目的に合わせた適切なアクセス権や振る舞いを指定できます。ファイルを開く際には、open() 関数の第二引数に適切なモード文字列を指定します。例えば、with open('file.txt', 'r') as file: のようにモードを指定してファイルを開くことができます。

さらに詳細なファイルモードをいくつか説明します：バイナリ読み込みモード（'rb'）:バイナリファイルを読み取るために使用されます（例：画像、音声ファイルなど）。ファイルはバイナリ形式で開かれ、テキストとしての解釈は行われません。バイナリデータを操作するためのメソッドや属性が利用可能です。バイナリ書き込みモード（'wb'）:バイナリファイルに書き込むために使用されます。ファイルが存在しない場合は新しいファイルが作成されます。バイナリデータを書き込むためのメソッドが利用可能です。バイナリ読み書きモード（'r+b'、'w+b'）:バイナリファイルを読み書きするために使用されます。ファイルが存在しない場合はエラーが発生します。読み取りと書き込みの両方が可能です。追記バイナリモード（'ab'、'a+b'）:バイナリファイルの末尾に追記するために使用されます。ファイルが存在しない場合は新しいファイルが作成されます。既存のデータが保持されたまま新しいデータが追加されます。これらのバイナリモードは、テキストデータではなくバイナリデータを読み書きする場合に使用されます。バイナリデータはテキストではないため、特殊な処理やエンコードが必要な場合があります。例えば、バイナリ読み込みモードでファイルを開くには、open('file.bin', 'rb') のように指定します。バイナリデータを読み書きする場合は、適切なバイナリモードを選択する必要があります。

The error message "Pull request creation failed. Validation failed: must be a collaborator" typically occurs in version control systems like Git and platforms like GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket. This error is related to the permissions and access controls for creating pull requests in a specific repository. Let's break down what it means and how to resolve it:Collaborator Status: In most version control platforms, repositories have a list of collaborators or contributors who have permission to make changes to the codebase and create pull requests. Only those who have been added as collaborators to the repository can create pull requests by default.User Access: If you encounter this error message, it means the user attempting to create the pull request is not listed as a collaborator for the repository. As a result, the system rejects the pull request creation request due to insufficient permissions.To resolve this issue, there are a few steps to take:Confirm Collaborator Status: Ensure that the user attempting to create the pull request is indeed listed as a collaborator for the repository. They should be explicitly added as a collaborator or part of a group/team that has access to the repository.Check Repository Permissions: If you're an administrator or owner of the repository, double-check the repository's settings to ensure that the user has the necessary permissions to create pull requests. If they are not a collaborator, add them to the list of collaborators.Fork and Create Pull Request: If the user does not have direct collaborator access to the repository, they can still contribute by forking the repository into their account. After making the changes in their forked repository, they can then submit a pull request from their fork to the original repository. The repository owner or a collaborator with sufficient permissions can then review and merge the changes.Organization Membership: If you're working in an organization account, ensure that the user is a member of the organization with the appropriate access rights. Organization-level permissions might override repository-level permissions.Personal Access Token: If the user is using a personal access token to authenticate, verify that the token has the necessary permissions to create pull requests.If you're encountering this issue while using a specific platform like GitHub or GitLab, it's also a good idea to consult their documentation or support resources for platform-specific troubleshooting.Remember that the exact steps to resolve this issue might vary based on the version control system or hosting platform you are using.

Creating secure authentication workflows can be a tricky business, but it's great that you're giving this a lot of thought. Here are some options you might consider:Use a dynamic, non-secret value as a salt: Instead of hard-coding the salt or including it in the link, you could derive it from some other value that you're already sending. For example, you could use a hashed version of the user's email as the salt. This would provide unique salts for each user without you having to store them anywhere. However, since the email address itself isn't secret, this wouldn't necessarily add a lot of security - it would primarily serve to thwart precomputed dictionary attacks ("rainbow tables").Include the salt in the link: While you're right that this reduces security somewhat, it might be a reasonable compromise given your requirements. A potential attacker would still need to break your encryption in order to use the link, and if your encryption is strong, this should be difficult. To make the links safer, consider using a secure random generator to produce the salt.Store the salt in a user session: This could work, but user sessions typically live on the server, so this would contradict your requirement of not touching the database (unless you're using a stateless JWT-style session, in which case you're back to sending the salt to the client).JWT tokens: You could use JSON Web Tokens (JWT) to create the magic links. JWTs are a compact, URL-safe means of representing claims to be transferred between two parties. You can include the user's email and an expiration time in the token, then sign it using a secret key. When the user clicks the link, you validate the token and, if it's valid and not expired, the email is verified. You don't need to store anything in the database, and there's no need for a salt because you're not hashing anything. The downside is that if an attacker gets your secret key, they can create valid tokens.TOTP for random numbers: If you're asking users to enter random numbers, consider using Time-based One-Time Password (TOTP) algorithm. It generates a one-time password based on the current time and a secret key. The server knows the secret key and can generate its own OTPs to compare with what the user entered. The nice thing about TOTP is that it automatically includes expiration (because the OTP changes over time), and if you only accept each OTP once, it can't be reused even if it's intercepted.In general, make sure to use secure, up-to-date cryptographic algorithms and libraries. Older algorithms and libraries may have known vulnerabilities that make your system easier to attack. Consider also rate limiting attempts to use the magic link to mitigate brute force attacks.

Option 1: This is a simple and effective approach for thwarting precomputed dictionary attacks, but keep in mind it is only as secure as the hash function you use. Since the salt isn't secret, a potential attacker could still make an offline attack if they get hold of your hashed data and know your algorithm. However, if you're using a strong encryption algorithm and a sufficiently complex key, this should be difficult.Option 2: There's not much difference in terms of security between options 1 and 2, but option 2 may be a bit simpler to implement. The main consideration here is that the salt should be randomly generated and sufficiently long to make guessing it impractical. Also, you should make sure that the generated links are only valid for a limited period of time to prevent their reuse if they are intercepted or leaked.Option 3: Putting the salt in a cookie would mean that it is tied to a specific browser, which could be inconvenient for users as you've noted. The risk of someone hacking into people's emails varies depending on the sensitivity of the data your app is handling. For most consumer applications, it's probably not a high risk, but it's not nonexistent either. If you're dealing with highly sensitive data, you might want to consider a more secure approach.Option 4: JWT tokens are signed but not encrypted by default, meaning the payload data can be read by anyone who intercepts the token. If an attacker has the secret key, they can forge tokens, which would be a problem. The key here is to keep the secret key secure. As for rainbow table attacks, they're more applicable to hashed values (like password hashes), not signed tokens like JWT. As long as you use a strong, secure secret key, rainbow attacks aren't really a concern for JWTs.Option 5: TOTP is a good solution, especially because it naturally prevents reuse of the code. However, typical TOTP codes are 6 digits long, which might be a bit long for users to type without errors. It could work in the query param for a magic link, but again, you would need to ensure that the magic link is used within a limited time frame. In practice, many services send TOTP codes via SMS or through an authenticator app. Remember, TOTP requires a shared secret between the server and the client. Implementing TOTP (Time-based One-Time Password) from scratch without using existing libraries is possible, but it's a non-trivial task. The TOTP algorithm is defined in RFC 6238, and involves a number of cryptographic operations, including HMAC-SHA1 hashing and Base32 encoding.Here's a rough outline of the steps you would need to follow:Generate a Secret Key: This will be a random binary string, typically 80 bits or longer. You could generate it using a cryptographically secure random number generator.Share the Secret Key: You need to securely share this secret key with the user. Often this is done by creating a QR code that the user can scan using an authenticator app.Generate the TOTP: This involves several steps:Calculate the number of time steps between an epoch (usually 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC) and the current time. The time step is typically 30 seconds.Convert this time step value to a byte array.Calculate the HMAC-SHA1 hash of this byte array, using the secret key.Perform some operations on this hash to convert it into a 6-digit number.Validate the TOTP: When the user provides a TOTP, you need to repeat the generation process and see if you get the same result.There are a number of complexities here, including handling time synchronization issues, ensuring all your cryptographic operations are secure, and dealing with different encodings and data types. Implementing these yourself can be error-prone and is generally not recommended unless you have a very good reason for doing so.If you're concerned about dependencies, one option could be to use a smaller, more focused library that only handles the HMAC-SHA1 and Base32 encoding parts, and implement the TOTP-specific parts yourself. But in general, using a well-maintained and widely-used library like speakeasy is going to be both safer and easier.

Using the same secret key for all users could pose a security risk. Here's why:The secret key is essentially the seed for the one-time password generation. If you're using the same secret key for all users, then the OTP generated at any given time will be the same for all users. This means that if an attacker manages to intercept or otherwise acquire a valid OTP, they could potentially use it to impersonate any user.Additionally, if the shared secret key were to be compromised (e.g., if an attacker gained access to your environment variables), they would be able to generate valid OTPs for any user. In contrast, if each user has a unique secret key, an attacker who compromises one key would only be able to impersonate that one user.That said, there may be scenarios where a shared key might be acceptable, depending on the specifics of your application and threat model. For example, if you're generating OTPs that are only used once and then immediately expired, and you have other layers of security in place, it might be less of a risk.However, it's generally considered best practice to use unique keys for each user to minimize the potential impact of a key being compromised.If you're looking to avoid creating a database table, one possibility might be to derive a unique secret key for each user based on some other unique attribute of the user (like their user ID or email), combined with a master key stored as an environment variable. But this has its own potential issues (for instance, you would need to handle key derivation securely), and in general it's still advisable to store per-user secret keys in a secure manner, which typically means a dedicated database table.

Given that you're open to using a database and want to maintain both the magic link and short code verification options, here's a proposed solution:Create a Database Table: You will need a table to store the secret keys for each user, along with the generated OTP, timestamp of OTP generation, and user's email. You might name it email_verification.On User Registration: During user registration or when the user asks for a magic link/OTP:Generate a random secret key for the user using a cryptographically secure random number generator. Store this in the email_verification table along with the user's email.Generate the OTP using TOTP methodology and the user's secret key. Store the OTP and the generation time in the email_verification table.Send the OTP to the user's email as part of a magic link or a separate code.On User Verification: When the user clicks on the magic link or enters the OTP:Fetch the OTP and timestamp from the email_verification table for that user's email.If the timestamp is too old (say, more than 10 minutes), reject the verification.If the user clicked a magic link, compare the OTP in the magic link with the OTP from the database. If they match, the verification is successful.If the user entered a code manually, compare the entered OTP with the OTP from the database. If they match, the verification is successful.After successful verification, you should delete the OTP entry from the email_verification table to avoid reusing it.On User Requesting a New OTP: When the user asks for a new OTP/magic link:Generate a new OTP as in step 2.Replace the old OTP and timestamp in the email_verification table with the new OTP and current timestamp.This way, you're not storing the OTP in a cookie or a URL, you're keeping the database as the single source of truth, and you're maintaining a secure, user-friendly authentication workflow.

You're correct in assuming that an attacker could potentially exploit the vulnerability of a hardcoded salt, but it's important to understand how and why this could happen.A salt is a random value that is generated for each instance of encryption, and it's usually concatenated with the password (or any other data you're encrypting) before the encryption process. This is particularly effective in preventing pre-computed dictionary attacks, commonly known as rainbow table attacks.A rainbow table attack works by pre-computing the hashes of all possible plaintexts and then storing them. An attacker can then simply look up the hash to get the plaintext. These are effective against systems where the same hash function is used across all records.Salting defends against this because it adds a unique value to each record, which means that pre-computed hashes are no longer effective. In this case, the attacker would need a unique rainbow table for each salt, which is computationally expensive and thus impractical.If you hardcode a salt, then you effectively have a system where the same salt is used across all records. This means an attacker only needs to compute a rainbow table once, which drastically reduces the complexity of an attack.Now, considering your case, where you're not storing the encrypted values anywhere, an attacker would have to intercept your encrypted tokens during transmission. This could happen through various methods, such as packet sniffing, man-in-the-middle attacks, or by gaining access to the email account where the tokens are sent.If the attacker has the encrypted token and the salt (which is hardcoded, and so could be found out by inspecting your system or through other means), then they could attempt a brute force attack to figure out the original payload, or use rainbow tables if the hashing function is known and the salt is the same across all tokens.The advantage of a time-limited token is that even if an attacker manages to intercept and decrypt a token, it will be useless after the expiration time, which adds an additional level of security. This reduces the time window in which an attacker can exploit a stolen token.As for an encryption method that uses a shared secret key and doesn't bother with a salt, you might want to look at symmetric encryption methods, such as AES. AES encryption is very strong and widely used. However, it still requires a key, which should be kept secure and definitely not hardcoded into your system.In summary, while it's true that your method is less susceptible to typical rainbow table attacks, it's still vulnerable to other forms of attacks, particularly if the attacker manages to gain access to your encryption key or your hardcoded salt. Adding unique, per-token salts and keeping your secret key secure will significantly improve the security of your system.

The server and the client both generate the TOTP independently and then the client sends its version to the server for verification. If the server's generated TOTP matches the client's TOTP, then the client is authenticated.A key aspect of this is that the shared secret must be securely stored and protected against unauthorized access. Key rotation is indeed a common practice in cryptography to mitigate the risk of key exposure. However, the effectiveness of key rotation in preventing brute-force attacks depends on a few factors:Rotation Frequency: The rotation frequency should be set according to the perceived risk and capability of the attacker. In theory, a higher rotation frequency can make brute-force attacks harder by reducing the time window an attacker has to crack the key. However, too frequent rotation may cause operational issues, and tokens generated with old keys will become invalid unless you maintain a grace period system.Grace Period: As you mentioned, maintaining a grace period during which tokens encrypted with old keys are still accepted can help with operational smoothness during key transitions. However, this also means that the effectiveness of key rotation in preventing brute-force attacks is somewhat reduced, as the time window for cracking the old key is extended.Key Strength: Key rotation can be less effective if the encryption keys are not strong enough to begin with. If your encryption key is weak or guessable, an attacker might be able to crack it before the next rotation.Rotating keys regularly can certainly increase the security of your system, but it's not a silver bullet. You still need to consider other potential vulnerabilities and security measures. For instance, key management and secure storage of keys become more critical in a system with frequent key rotation. If an attacker can access your new keys (e.g., by compromising the system where keys are generated or stored), key rotation won't help much.Another potential vulnerability could be if an attacker is able to intercept the communication between the server and the client (e.g., man-in-the-middle attack). This could reveal not just the encrypted tokens, but also other sensitive information. Therefore, it's important to secure the communication channels as well, e.g., using HTTPS for web traffic.Additionally, secure handling of email communication is critical since the OTP is sent via email. If an attacker can intercept or access the user's email, they can get the OTP. Therefore, secure email practices, such as using secure email servers and encouraging users to use strong email passwords and two-factor authentication, can also be helpful.Lastly, remember that no system is perfectly secure. The goal is to make attacking the system more costly (in terms of time, effort, and resources) than the potential gain from the attack. A layered approach to security, which combines several security measures, can help achieve this goal.

In the Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM), the terms "slot" and "word" are not exactly the same, and they should not be used interchangeably.A "slot" refers to a unit of storage on the EVM. Each slot is 32 bytes (or 256 bits) in size. The EVM's storage is a key-value store where each key is a 256-bit number and each value is a 256-bit number, where the key can be thought of as the slot's index and the value is what is stored in that slot.On the other hand, a "word" in EVM terminology is also a 32-byte (256-bit) unit, but it is used in a different context. "Words" often refer to units of data used in memory or on the stack, as well as for the data passed to and returned by function calls. When EVM instructions operate on data, they do so on these "words".So, while both "slots" and "words" are 256-bit units, they are used in different contexts - "slots" for storage and "words" for data manipulation, memory, and function calls. They are not generally referred to interchangeably. Calling a storage slot an "EVM word" could cause confusion.

The time complexity for this function can be broken down as follows:Step 1: Constructing the word frequency dictionary. This step involves iterating over every event and every word in each event title. Given n events and an average of m words per event, this step has a time complexity of O(n * m).Step 2: Constructing the bigram frequency dictionary. This is similar to step 1, but now we're considering pairs of words rather than individual words. Despite this, the time complexity remains O(n * m) since we're still iterating over every event and nearly every word.Step 3: Checking for bigram overlap. This step involves iterating over every bigram and performing a constant amount of work for each (looking up the durations of the constituent words and the bigram itself, performing a few arithmetic operations, and potentially adding a new key-value pair to the words dictionary and deleting two others). Therefore, this step has a time complexity of O(p), where p is the total number of bigrams.Given that p is directly proportional to n * m (since a bigram is formed from every pair of adjacent words in each event), we can say that the time complexity of the entire function is O(n * m).In the case of 1,000 events with 5 words each, this should generally be manageable. However, keep in mind that the actual runtime will depend on a variety of factors, including the specific performance characteristics of the system running the code.

تنصل من المسؤولية

تم تحديث آخر مرة في: 10 يناير 2020

التفسير والتعريفات

التفسير

الكلمات التي تبدأ بحرف كبير لها معانٍ محددة في الشروط التالية.

تعريفات الوصول الواحد تحمل نفس المعنى بغض النظر عما إذا كانت في صيغة المفرد أم الجمع.

التعريفات

لأغراض هذا التنصل من المسؤولية:

  • الشركة (المشار إليها في هذا سياسة الكوكيز باسم "الشركة" أو "نحن" أو "لنا") تشير إلى myPlanet.
  • أنت تعني الفرد الذي يستخدم الخدمة، أو الشركة، أو الكيان القانوني الآخر الذي يستخدم الخدمة نيابة عن هذا الفرد، حسب الاقتضاء.
  • التطبيق يعني برنامج البرمجيات الذي قدمته الشركة وتم تنزيله بواسطتك على أي جهاز إلكتروني يحمل اسم myPlanet.
  • الخدمة تشير إلى التطبيق.

تنصل من المسؤولية

المعلومات الواردة في الخدمة هي لأغراض عامة فقط.

الشركة لا تتحمل أي مسؤولية عن الأخطاء أو الغفوات في محتويات الخدمة.

في أي حال من الأحوال، لا تكون الشركة مسؤولة عن أي أضرار خاصة أو مباشرة أو غير مباشرة أو تبعية أو عرضية أو أي أضرار أخرى، سواء كانت في إطار عقد أو إهمال أو غير ذلك من القضايا القانونية، تنشأ عن استخدام الخدمة أو محتويات الخدمة. تحتفظ الشركة بالحق في إضافة أو حذف أو تعديل المحتويات في الخدمة في أي وقت دون إشعار مسبق.

لا تضمن الشركة أن الخدمة خالية من الفيروسات أو المكونات الضارة الأخرى.

تنصل من معلومات الرعاية الصحية

المعلومات المقدمة بواسطة الخدمة حول الصحة ليست مقصودة لتشخيص أو علاج أو علاج أو منع الأمراض. يتم توفير المنتجات والخدمات والمعلومات والمحتوى الآخر المقدمة من خلال الخدمة، بما في ذلك المعلومات المرتبطة بمواقع الويب الأخرى، لأغراض إعلامية فقط.

المعلومات المقدمة من خلال الخدمة ليست شاملة ولا تغطي جميع الأمراض أو الأوجاع أو الحالات الطبية أو علاجها.

الأفراد مختلفون وقد يتفاعلون بشكل مختلف مع منتجات مختلفة. التعليقات التي يدلي بها الموظفون أو المستخدمون الآخرون على الخدمة هي آراءهم الشخصية الخاصة التي تعبر عن آرائهم الشخصية الخاصة ولا تمثل موقف أو وجهة نظر الشركة.

لا تتحمل الشركة أي مسؤولية عن أي معلومات يتم توفيرها من خلال الخدمة فيما يتعلق بتوصيات بشأن المكملات لأي أغراض صحية.

لا تقدم الشركة أي ضمان أو ضمان بشأن أي منتجات أو خدمات مباعة. الشركة ليست مسؤولة عن أي أضرار ناتجة عن المعلومات أو الخدمات المقدمة حتى إذا تم تنبيه الشركة إلى إمكانية حدوث أضرار.

تنصل من المسؤولية بشأن الروابط الخارجية

قد تحتوي الخدمة على روابط إلى مواقع ويب خارجية لا تقدمها أو تحتفظ بها الشركة بأي طريقة.

يرجى ملاحظة أن الشركة لا تضمن دقة أو صلة أو توقيت أو اكتمال أي معلومات على هذه المواقع الخارجية.

تنصل من المسؤولية عن الأخطاء والغفوات

تتمثل معلومات الخدمة في إرشادات عامة حول مسائل ذات أهمية فقط. حتى إذا اتخذت الشركة كل احتياطات لضمان أن محتوى الخدمة سارٍ ودقيق، قد تحدث أخطاء. بالإضافة إلى ذلك، ونظرًا للطبيعة المتغيرة للقوانين والقواعد واللوائح، قد تحدث تأخيرات أو حذفات أو عدم دقة في المعلومات الموجودة في الخدمة.

لا تتحمل الشركة أي مسؤولية عن أي أخطاء أو غفوات، أو عن النتائج المتحققة من استخدام هذه المعلومات.

تنصل من الاستخدام العادل

قد يستخدم الشركة مواد محمية بحقوق الطبع والنشر والتي لم يتم تفويضها دائمًا بشكل صريح من قبل مالك حقوق الطبع والنشر. تتيح الشركة هذه المواد المحمية بحقوق الطبع والنشر للانتقاد والتعليق ونشر الأخبار والتدريس والبحوث العلمية أو الأكاديمية.

تعتقد الشركة أن هذا يشكل "استخدامًا عادلاً" لأي مواد محمية بحقوق الطبع والنشر من هذا النوع كما هو موضح في القسم 107 من قانون حقوق الطبع والنشر في الولايات المتحدة.

إذا كنت ترغب في استخدام المواد المحمية بحقوق الطبع والنشر من الخدمة لأغراضك الشخصية التي تتجاوز الاستخدام العادل، يجب عليك الحصول على إذن من مالك حقوق الطبع والنشر.

تنصل من المسؤولية عن الآراء المعبر عنها

قد تحتوي الخدمة على آراء وآراء هي للمؤلفين ولا تعكس بالضرورة السياسة الرسمية أو الموقف الرسمي لأي مؤلف آخر أو وكالة أو منظمة أو صاحب عمل أو شركة، بما في ذلك الشركة.

التعليقات التي ينشرها المستخدمون هي مسؤوليتهم الشخصية فقط، وسيتحمل المستخدمون المسؤولية الكاملة والمسؤولية واللوم عن أي قذف أو دعوى قانونية ناتجة عن شيء مكتوب في تعليق أو نتيجة مباشرة لشيء مكتوب في تعليق. الشركة غير مسؤولة عن أي تعليق ينشره المستخدمون وتحتفظ بالحق في حذف أي تعليق لأي سبب كان.

تنصل من المسؤولية عن عدم التحمل

تم توفير المعلومات في الخدمة مع الفهم بأن الشركة ليست مشغولة هنا في تقديم الاستشارة والمشورة القانونية والمحاسبية والضريبية أو غيرها من المشورة والخدمات المهنية. على هذا النحو، لا يجب استخدامها كبديل للاستشارة مع مستشاري المحاسبة والضرائب والقانونية أو غيرها من المستشارين المختصين.

في أي حال من الأحوال، لا تكون الشركة أو مورديها مسؤولين عن أي أضرار خاصة أو عرضية أو غير مباشرة أو تبعية تنشأ عن استخدامك للخدمة أو عدم القدرة على الوصول إليها أو استخدامها.

تنصل من "استخدام على مسؤوليتك الخاصة"

جميع المعلومات المقدمة في الخدمة هي "كما هي"، دون ضمان كامل للمعلومات الكاملة أو الدقة أو الاتساق أو النتائج التي تم الحصول عليها من استخدام هذه المعلومات، ودون أي ضمان صريح أو ضمني، بما في ذلك، على سبيل المثال لا الحصر، ضمانات الأداء أو التسويق أو اللياقة لغرض معين.

لن تكون الشركة مسؤولة تجاهك أو تجاه أي شخص آخر عن أي قرار تتخذه أو أي إجراء تتخذه بالاعتماد على المعلومات المقدمة من خلال الخدمة أو عن أي أضرار تبعية أو خاصة مماثلة، حتى إذا تم تنبيه الشركة إلى إمكانية حدوث مثل تلك الأضرار.

اتصل بنا

إذا كان لديك أي أسئلة حول هذا التنصل من المسؤولية، يمكنك الاتصال بنا:

  • عن طريق زيارة هذه الصفحة على موقعنا على الويب: https://ole.org/contact

ماي بلانت

ماي بلانت هو أداة تعليمية مصممة للعمل مع تطبيق ويب بلانت. تم استخدامه لتحسين التعليم المبكر، والمدارس الثانوية، وصحة القرى، وتنمية قوى العمل الشبابية، والتنمية الاقتصادية والمجتمعية.

بلانت هاوس هو مستودع للموارد المجانية ومفتوحة الوصول والمجال العام لصالح جميع المتعلمين.

تم تصميم ماي بلانت ليكون متاحًا للجميع، في كل مكان، في كل وقت. إنه قابل للنقل وبأسعار معقولة وقابل للتوسع ومستدام. يعمل على أي جهاز أندرويد مثل الأجهزة اللوحية والهواتف المحمولة. يعمل مع أو بدون اتصال بالإنترنت.

يتيح هذا التطبيق للمدارس والمجتمعات الحصول على مكتبة ونظام تعلم متعدد الوسائط كامل يتصل ببلانت بشكل دوري. يمكن أن تحتوي الأجهزة المكونة على لوحة القيادة الشخصية للمتعلمين. يتأكد هذا من قدرة المتعلمين على قراءة الكتب على رفهم وأخذ الدورات بدون اتصال - أي بدون اتصال بخادم مركزي. يتم تشجيع المتعلمين على تقييم الموارد والدورات التي يستخدمونها من خلال نظام تصنيف من واحد إلى خمس نجوم. يمكن للمتعلمين بشكل دوري مزامنة بياناتهم مع الخادم. يتم تحميل بيانات الأنشطة وتحميل الموارد الجديدة في غضون دقائق قليلة إلى ماي بلانت للاستخدام دون اتصال.

تحتوي لوحة القيادة أيضًا على سجل إنجازات وتقويم أحداث ونظام محادثة داخلي للتواصل مع أعضاء الفريق.

ثبت أن ماي بلانت فعالة للغاية في تحسين فرص التعلم لأكثر من خمسين ألف متعلم في أكثر من 100 موقع، في المدارس في جميع أنحاء نيبال وغانا وكينيا ورواندا، مع اللاجئين السوريين في الأردن، واللاجئين الصوماليين في كينيا، وعمال الصحة في القرى في أوغندا.

In the context of the Spotify API, SpotifyClientCredentials and SpotifyOAuth are two different authorization flows used to authenticate and authorize access to Spotify's resources.SpotifyClientCredentials:
SpotifyClientCredentials is a simple and straightforward authorization flow suitable for server-to-server authentication. It relies on client credentials, which consist of a client ID and a client secret. With this flow, you authenticate your application as a whole rather than authenticating individual users. The client ID and secret are obtained by registering your application with the Spotify Developer Dashboard. Once authenticated, your application can access public resources on Spotify, such as retrieving playlists or albums.However, with SpotifyClientCredentials, you don't have access to user-specific resources or actions, like modifying playlists or accessing a user's playback state. This flow is primarily used for applications that don't require individual user permissions and operate on public data.SpotifyOAuth:
